findings.control: At 44ab7c4 on the cloud VM with MuJoCo's default-for-this-guest EGL renderer (MUJOCO_GL=egl, as every cloud room run since the closeout) the control reproduces history for seed 1013 only (116.02 s, same tool calls). Seeds 2000 and 2004 fail at the control itself (2000: 'candidate 8 has a handle, but no reachable viewpoint', 163.1 s; 2004: explored the reachable space, no handle, 171.3 s). With MUJOCO_GL=osmesa on the same VM the control reproduces history exactly on all three seeds (sim_s, path_m, tool-call sequence and contact steps identical to results/g1_explore_room rows). The Windows laptop (glfw) also reproduces 2004 exactly and 1013/2000 as successes. So the historical result is reproducible, but only under software (OSMesa) rendering; under EGL on the L4 the rendered frames differ enough to change what the agent perceives (in 2004 the handle of candidate 1 is never detected under EGL, 0 views, against 8 views under OSMesa from the same poses).

seed_1013.flip_commit: b8208bb (Fix instance-bound inspection recovery and isolate camera delivery)
seed_1013.evidence: outcome flips between 34167bc and b8208bb in all three environments (cloud EGL, cloud OSMesa, Windows glfw) and stays failed at 12a9d15, 5b02731, 13e4c95, a3b4304; ARRIVAL_MARGIN (5b02731) changes nothing (1fce5c5 identical to a3b4304 on the cloud EGL arm).
seed_1013.mechanism: Identical trajectory through the first inspect. 34167bc: the inspect at step 6 happens 1.46 m from the handle (limit 1.4 m); the next approach (side 4) moves the robot into the valid band, verify_goal then passes because the earlier inspection's handle_confirmed_close flag is still set (confirmation and pose check at different poses); the independent scorer confirms a true success. b8208bb: inspect succeeds only if the inspect itself happens at a valid inspection pose, and side_point now returns the cheapest reachable cell in the band [0.6, 1.4] m instead of a point 1.0 m from the handle. The robot is already near the handle, so the cheapest cell is the near edge (0.6 m); the 0.1 m arrival error lands it at 0.42-0.57 m (below the 0.6 m lower bound) on every retry: six approach/inspect pairs, each 'partial observation only: 0.5 m from the handle', until the 240 s budget (or 'no reachable viewpoint' once approach counts are used up). The 5b02731 margin only shrinks the upper bound, so it cannot help.
seed_1013.ablation: on b8208bb with one hunk group reverted (not tested commits): reverting only the side_point rewrite restores success (119.7 s); reverting only the viewpoints() side filter or only the stricter inspection_complete does not (fail); reverting all three restores the pre-b8208bb run exactly (116.02 s, 15.96 m).
seed_1013.classification: defect (unintended regression in viewpoint selection, with the stricter inspection rule exposing it). Not chaos: the flip is at the same commit in three environments, and at current code 3 of the 4 one-millimetre start shifts still fail (cloud EGL jx and jy, Windows jx) while 44ab7c4 succeeds under all 4. One shifted run (Windows jy, a3b4304) succeeds by taking a different route (the first inspect then lands in the valid band), so the defect is route-dependent rather than certain. The stricter rule alone is a deliberate trade-off (the old success relied on a stale confirmation flag) but it is not what fails the seed.

seed_2000.flip_commit: none under history-faithful rendering; b8208bb on the Windows laptop; not defined on cloud EGL because the control already fails
seed_2000.evidence: OSMesa cloud: control 239.42 s reproduces history and every tested commit (34167bc ... a3b4304) also succeeds, at 239.4-239.8 s against a 240 s budget (the budget is only checked between actions, so these are 0.2 s from failing). Windows glfw: succeeds through 34167bc (207.7 s) and fails from b8208bb (282.7 s / 241.8 s time budget). Cloud EGL: fails at every commit; failure text changes at b8208bb from 'candidate 8 ...' to 'candidate 5 ... no reachable viewpoint' with the same 0.42-0.46 m 'too close to the handle' inspect loop as seed 1013.
seed_2000.mechanism: A time-budget-marginal seed. Where the handle is found early enough (glfw, EGL) the b8208bb side_point edge-of-band loop of seed 1013 appears and consumes the budget; under OSMesa the handle (candidate 17) is only found at step 13 and the single approach to it ends in the valid band, so it passes with 0.2 s to spare at the control and at current code.
seed_2000.perturbation: cloud EGL, 1 mm start shift at 44ab7c4: 2000 fails unshifted but succeeds shifted in x (145.1 s) and in y (127.1 s); at a3b4304 it fails under both shifts. Windows glfw: a3b4304 2000 fails unshifted and succeeds with the x shift (158.1 s, identical to 44ab7c4 with that shift) and with the y shift.
seed_2000.classification: chaotic sensitivity / environment (rendering backend), with the seed-1013 defect contributing where it is reached. Not a clean code regression.

seed_2004.flip_commit: none: its outcome is the same at every tested commit in every environment
seed_2004.evidence: cloud EGL fails at all 14 commits (171.3 s); cloud OSMesa succeeds at both endpoints (70.82 s); Windows glfw succeeds at all 14 commits; the A1 closeout failure is therefore the EGL renderer, not a commit. 1 mm start shift under EGL: 44ab7c4 jx fails (186.6 s), jy succeeds (70.4 s); a3b4304 the same. Windows: 44ab7c4 jy fails.
seed_2004.mechanism: Rendering backend: under EGL the handle of candidate 1 is never detected (0 views) from poses where OSMesa detects it, so the room is exhausted without a handle.
seed_2004.classification: environment (rendering backend) plus chaotic sensitivity; not a code regression.

findings.A3_lite_margin_0: Current code with ARRIVAL_MARGIN = 0 (1fce5c5) gives the same outcome as a3b4304 on all three seeds on cloud EGL (1013 fail 243.0 s, 2000 fail 215.5 s, 2004 fail 171.3 s, all identical to a3b4304), and the same two failures plus the 2004 success on Windows glfw. The OSMesa run of 1fce5c5 was queued last and not reached.
findings.implication: Every cloud room result since the closeout (A1, A2, the frozen g1_explore_room_closeout) ran under MUJOCO_GL=egl, while the historical g1_explore_room ran under software rendering. The renderer changes outcomes by itself (2000 and 2004 fail at the unchanged 44ab7c4 under EGL). Part of the frozen 15/20 and 4/10 may be renderer effect rather than code; this was not tested here and needs the owner's decision.
